answer.policy_title: Femoroacetabular Impingement Surgery, Surgery Policy No. 160 (SUR160)
criteria_quotes: A. Moderate-to-severe hip pain that is worsened by flexion activities (e.g., squatting or prolonged sitting) that significantly limits activities

B. Unresponsive to conservative therapy for at least 3 months or clinical documentation that conservative therapy is contraindicated (e.g., history of falls due to mechanical instability of hip joint)
C. Positive impingement sign on clinical examination (i.e., pain elicited with 90 degrees of flexion and internal rotation and adduction of the femur)
1. Imaging (conventional x-rays, MRI, MRI arthrogram) documents morphology indicative of cam-type or pincer-type FAI (See List of Information Needed for Review); and
2. No evidence of advanced osteoarthritis, defined as Tonnis grade II or III, or joint space of less than 2 mm, except when there is mechanical instability.
E. Requested procedures must be consistent with the anatomical abnormalities documented.
• History and Physical • Documented symptoms and conservative treatments attempted specific to policy criteria 1. B. • Physical exam findings
• Imaging (conventional x-rays, MRI, MRI arthrogram) that documents morphology indicative of cam-type or pincer-type FAI such as one or more of the following:
ii. femoral head-neck offset with an alpha angle greater than 50 degrees
iv. acetabular retroversion (overcoverage with crossover sign)
v. coxa profunda or protrusion vi. damage of the acetabular rim
answer.submission_route: Regence publishes a separate appeal form for each state on its member appeals page. Download YOUR state's form there; the Oregon form returns to the Lewiston, ID PO box or by fax.
